Q1: What should this heal issue deliver?
Choices:
A) No code change. Record the cause as transient or environmental, re-trigger `/approved` on #10048, and close this issue. Pick this if the run-window check under Q3 shows other runs recovered.
B) Add a bounded retry to the memory clone reads only: the fast-path clone in `_clone_for_memory_branch`, `_full_repo_clone_for_memory_branch` and `read_memory_root_from_branch`. Retry on a bare `returned error: 403` and on `returned error: 5xx`, at most 3 attempts with jittered backoff and about 30 s in total. After the last attempt, still raise `MemoryGitError` so the claim fails closed. The push policy that never retries a bare 403 stays unchanged. Add regression tests for "403 once, then success" and "403 every time, claim still exits non-zero". (RECOMMENDED)
C) Same as B, but retry only on 5xx and on a 403 whose text names a rate limit or abuse, matching the push policy. Note: this would not have recovered run 45408016593, because its log has no rate-limit text.
D) Diagnostics only: when a memory clone fails, always print the first stderr line of the single-branch probe (with credentials and URLs removed), even without `AI_MEMORY_CLONE_DIAGNOSTICS=1`. Add no retry.
Q2: Q1:B, C and D all need edits to `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, which is outside the heal-scope `paths=` list. How should scope be handled?
Choices:
A) Widen the scope for this issue to add `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`. The existing `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md` entries already cover tests and changelog. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Keep the current scope. Put any hardening only in `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, for example a bounded step-level retry around `memory_processed_command_claim` in the "Claim /approved command" step. Note: incompatible with Q1:D, which can only be done in `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`.
C) Not applicable. Q1:A was chosen and no files change.
Q3: What did the operator check of `GH_PAT` and of the runs around 14:00–14:15 UTC on 2026-11-24 show?
Choices:
A) Other runs using `GH_PAT` for git also got 403s in that window and later runs recovered, so it was throttling. The PAT was not changed. Pair with Q1:A or Q1:B. (RECOMMENDED)
B) `GH_PAT` was rotated, revoked or narrowed that day. This needs an operator fix to the secret, and no code change would have helped. Pair with Q1:A. Note: incompatible with Q1:B and Q1:C, because a retry cannot fix a bad credential.
C) Not checked or unknown. Go ahead with the Q1 choice as a defensive change, and state in the plan that the root cause is still unconfirmed.
